items.title: Write rate limiter: partition on the API key header so buckets exist before auth runs

seededDefectKey.scenario: An attacker scripts POSTs, each carrying a different made-up X-Api-Key value (trk_guess_0001, trk_guess_0002, ...).
seededDefectKey.consequence: Every distinct garbage key gets its own fresh fixed window, so none of the requests is ever throttled (all 401, never 429): the limiter stops slowing key-guessing entirely.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The same flood keeps running for hours with unique header values.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The partitioned limiter keeps one limiter per partition key, and the key space is now attacker-chosen, so the number of partitions held in memory is unbounded.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The shipped code partitions exactly this way.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Senior-review finding 1 (Medium): the patch reverts the proposed fix back to the reviewed defect.
